full_judgment:
5. The trial court decreed the suit. It declared the plaintiff's right, title and interest to 2/3rd share of schedule Kha and Ga land and ordered that they were entitled under section 4 of the Partition Act to repurchase the remaining share on payment of Tk. 1,000/- by 13-8-73 in default their claim under section 4 of the Partition Act would stand cancelled and they would get only 2/3rd share of their Own. 

 6. The lower appellate court affirmed the order as to 2/3rd share but it modified the order as to option to repurchase under section 4 of the Partition Act. It ordered that the plaintiffs would be entitled to repurchase 1/3rd share of the schedule land and the structures thereon that stood transferred to defendant No.1 at a price to be fixed by the court after appointing a Pleader Commissioner within 30 days of the order and after considering the existing valuation of the lands and structures the court would decide the value at which the questioned property be repurchased by the plaintiffs and then the final decree be passed to give effect to the order. 

 7. At the outset Mr. A.N.M. Shahidullah, the learned Advocate for the respondent, pointed out from the record that as there was no interim order from this court staying the order of the lower appellate court the final decree in the matter had already been sealed and signed on 2nd December, 1974, and thus, he submitted, that the appeal became infructuous do not find any substance in this submission. Long ago in a Full Bench decision of the Patna High Court in Musamat Bibi Wahidunnisa, V. Baba Deep Narain Prasad, 20 C.W.N., 1174 it was held that an appeal from a preliminary decree in partition suit could be heard although a final decree had been passed in the case and no appeal had been filed against the final decree. 

 8. Later in a Full Bench decision of the Calcutta High Court in Taleb Ali and anr V. Abdul Aziz and ors, 34 C.W.N. 46 it was held that an appeal from a preliminary decree did not become incompetent by reason of a final decree having been passed before the appeal was presented. Rankin C.J. who delivered the judgment also observed:— 

 "When a preliminary decree is set aside, the final decree is superseded, whether the appeal was brought before or after the passing of the final decree, and the Appellate Court when setting aside or varying a preliminary decree, can and should, give direction for the setting aside or varying the final decree, if the existence of such decree be brought to its notice as in all cases it should be." 

 11. Mr. A.H. Md. Saadat AB Khan, the learned Advocate for the appellant, has endeavoured to reopen the concurrent finding of fact that the plaintiff No. 2 was not a minor at the time of execution of Ext. A. I do not find any substance in this appeal. I uphold the judgment and decree of the court of appeal below and dismiss the appeal with costs.
